The first transfer window is from 29 November 2018 to 20 February 2019. ==Club licensing regulations== Since the [[2018 Malaysia Super League]] season, as part of the privatization effort, every team in the Liga Super Malaysia must have an FAM Club Licence{{cite web|url=http://www.fam.org.my/club-licensing-malaysia|title=Club Licensing in Malaysia – FAM|work=fam.org.my|access-date=28 March 2017|archive-date=2 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402075225/http://www.fam.org.my/club-licensing-malaysia|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://footballmalaysia.com/files/Club%20Licensing.pdf|title=Why Club Licensing? – footballmalaysia|website=FootballMalaysia.com|access-date=14 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330224745/http://footballmalaysia.com/files/Club%20Licensing.pdf|archive-date=30 March 2016|url-status=dead}} to play in the league or be relegated. To obtain an FAM Club Licence, teams must be financially healthy and meet certain standards of conduct as organisations. As in other national leagues, there are significant benefits to being in the top division: *A greater share of television broadcast licence revenues goes to Liga Super Malaysia sides. *Greater exposure through television and higher attendance levels helps Liga Super Malaysia teams attract the most lucrative sponsorship. *Liga Super Malaysia teams develop substantial financial muscle through the combination of television and gate revenues, sponsorship and marketing of their team brands. This allows them to attract and retain skilled players from domestic and international sources and to construct first-class stadium facilities. Despite several reminders from FAM from the beginning of 2015, however there are few teams failed to get the approval for both AFC and FAM club licenses from First Instance Body (FIB) .{{Cite web|url=https://www.fam.org.my/news/7-pasukan-lulus-lesen-kelab-untuk-liga-super-2018|title=7 PASUKAN LULUS LESEN KELAB UNTUK LIGA SUPER 2018|date=7 September 2017|website=FAM.org.my|publisher=Football Association of Malaysia|access-date=15 November 2017}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.fam.org.my/news/kedah-kelantan-melaka-lulus-lesen-kelab-fam-untuk-beraksi-pada-liga-super-2018|title=KEDAH, KELANTAN & MELAKA LULUS LESEN KELAB FAM UNTUK BERAKSI PADA LIGA SUPER 2018|date=2 November 2017|website=FAM.org.my|publisher=Football Association of Malaysia|access-date=15 November 2017}} {| class="wikitable sortable" !Team(s) !AFC Club License Status !FAM Club License Status |- |[[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[Perak TBG F.C.|Perak]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[PKNS F.C.|PKNS]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[Pahang FA|Pahang]] |Banned |Passed |- |[[Terengganu FC|Terengganu]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[Kedah FA|Kedah]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[Melaka United]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[Selangor FA|Selangor]] |Passed |Passed |- |[[PKNP F.C.|PKNP]] |Failed |Passed |- |[[Kuala Lumpur FA|Kuala Lumpur]] |Failed |Passed |- |[[FELDA United F.C.|Felda United]] |N/A |Passed |- |[[Petaling Jaya City FC|Petaling Jaya]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nst.com.my/sports/football/2019/01/451284/move-over-mifa-pj-city-fc-are-town|title=Move over MIFA, PJ City FC are in town|date=16 January 2019|website=New Straits Times Online|access-date=16 January 2019}} |N/A |Passed |} ''*Updated: 2 January 2019'' ==Team changes== [[Kelantan FA|Kelantan]] and [[Negeri Sembilan FA|Negeri Sembilan]] were relegated to [[2019 Malaysia Premier League]] after finished 11th and bottom place of [[2018 Malaysia Super League|last season league]].
